title: Memory
markdown:
**What it is:** What the Executive knows and where it came from, and what it does on its own. Two tabs: **What it knows** and **What it does**.

**When it remembers something:** under a reply, **Memory updated** says what it just kept (a fact, a decision, a figure, a note). Tap it to see each one, **Undo** any of them, or **See in Memory**. When something new is kept, a dot shows on **Memory**, and the page opens with **New since your last visit**, with **Undo** on each.

**What it knows:**

The top line says how many things it learned this week and how often it used what it knows.

- **About you**: what it learned from talking with you and from replies you approved. Only you see it. **Remove** any line that's wrong. **What you said** shows the newest notes it keeps of your own words, and opens them all.
- **About the company**: everything it knows about the business in one list. Each line says where it came from: **You told me** (facts, corrections and decisions you asked it to keep; they hold in every conversation, email, brief, scheduled run and alert review, and a decision shows its outcome once it's known), **I worked it out** (figures from its own work, such as a balance it read from a statement, with where each came from; only you see yours) or **Project** (what it's tracking, as planned, active, paused or completed). Pick one to see only that kind. **Remove** a line that's wrong, or open it to edit it.
- **What I learned**: the lessons it keeps, each with where it was used, such as "used 6 times: 3 in chat, 2 in email, 1 in a brief". A lesson is used everywhere the Executive works for you: chat, calls, the email it answers, the email it writes as you, your briefs and the work it starts on its own. **Remove** one to stop it. **How it's going** opens the rest: after a chat goes quiet, the Executive checks its own answers from your words and your reactions (a correction, a 👎, a reply you stopped, a turn you asked again). From that it keeps **lessons**: one line each, in your own words (a term you use, something you always want included, a thing to do rather than promise, which specialist to ask). It reads a lesson on later chats about the same thing and keeps count of how those went; one that doesn't help stops on its own and is listed under **Stopped saying it**. A lesson applies only to the chats of the person it was learned from. It can be about anything you said, mail included; it never lets the Executive send or share anything on its own. Each night the Executive reruns the answers it could have done better with everything it has learned since, in a dry run nobody receives (it reads for real but sends, books and saves nothing), and a judge says whether each would now go right. The ones that now do are listed under **Now gets right**. Each person sees their own. The owner also sees the ones from channels and group chats, never a teammate's own chat with the Executive, which stays theirs as it does everywhere else.

**What it does:**

- The **heartbeat**: the last 90 days beside what it did today, how long until the next thing it does, and how many days in a row it has been active. **More detail** opens the rest.
- **Left out of your brief** (owner only): lines your morning brief or end-of-day digest left out in the last day because they named people or figures the Executive couldn't match to your data. **Hide** clears it.
- **Coming up**: the next few briefs, check-ins and follow-ups. **Full schedule** shows them all, with background scans under **Show background scans**; choose **Cancel follow-up** in a follow-up's **⋯** to drop it.
- **Done for you**: this month's count in one line (owner only; click it for every count by month or week, against the period before), then the last few things it did, each saying what came of it, with **Read it** where it wrote something up and **See changes** on a day it kept your contacts up to date. **All activity** shows the full feed.

**How to use:**

1. Just chat. Projects are picked up from your conversations after each chat, a decision you make in chat is kept with what you taught it, and figures it works out from your documents are kept under **What it worked out**. There's nothing to add by hand.
2. Click **Memory** in the sidebar. **What it knows** opens first; each group shows a few rows, and **All N** opens the full list on its own screen. **Memory** at the top takes you back.
3. On **About the company**'s list, choose **Edit** in a project's **⋯** menu to change its title, summary or status, or **Delete** to remove it. It asks first; this can't be undone.
4. On **What it worked out**, choose **Edit** to correct a figure or what it's about, or **Remove**, then confirm on the row.
5. On **Your notes**, search with **Search your notes**, and use a note's **⋯**: **Correct**, **Pin** / **Unpin**, **Don't remember this** (forgets every note from that conversation and never notes it again) or **Forget** (deletes that one note). Both ask first and can't be undone.
6. On **Learning**, a **Getting better** card shows the lessons in use, how many times they were used in chats and the things it now gets right. **How I learn** opens the four steps (you chat, it looks back 30 minutes later, it keeps a lesson, it checks itself each night). Below it, **What I learned** and **Now gets right** switch between the lessons and the answers it now gets right. Each lesson says how many chats it was used in, and **not helping yet** when those chats went worse more often than fine. Click a row to see where it came from and **See the conversation**. To clear several at once, tick their boxes (or **Select all**, or, on lessons, **Select the N not helping**) and choose **Stop saying** (**Forget** on **Now gets right**). **Undo** brings them back for a few seconds; after that a forgotten row is gone. Retired lessons are under **Show N stopped**.
7. To correct a fact, just say it in chat — *"Maple House is 48 units, not 52"* or *"we're 42 people now"*. The Executive keeps it (a company-profile field such as headcount or burn updates the profile too), and it shows under **What you taught it** with your words. Choose **Edit** in a correction's **⋯** menu to change what it says (the old wording stays as what it corrects), or **Retire (stop using it)** when it no longer holds (it asks first); a company-profile change is fixed on the Company profile instead. Older, retired and declined versions stay under **Show history (N)**. You can also email a correction from your own address: nothing changes until you reply CONFIRM to the confirmation email the Executive sends you. Teammates on your People list can correct facts too, from the web app or their own Slack or Discord. Theirs are marked with their name and wait for your approval at the top of that list with **Approve** and **Decline** (the group says how many), and they appear in your morning brief. Under **Teammates' corrections**, untick **needs my approval** next to a teammate you trust to let theirs apply straight away; one that would replace yours still waits for you. Only you can retire someone else's correction.

**Example:** tell the Executive *"we've decided to push the EU launch to Q2 so we can finish SOC 2 first."* It keeps that as a decision under **What you taught it**, and the weekly review later asks how it turned out. If it's worded wrong, choose **Edit** in its **⋯** menu.

**Just for yourself?** When you use Open Executive just for yourself, the heartbeat leaves out department check-ins and the "Awaiting people" list, and the count of active projects takes the department check-ins' place under **More detail**. The same projects appear on Home under **Your projects**.

Advice from before it kept figures stays readable under **Older advice** at the bottom of **What it knows**.
